title: Quantitative Generalization Bounds for Multi-Layer Transformers: A Few Long Strings can Beat Many Short Ones
abstract: arXiv:2610.35715v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Transformer-based language models exhibit an astonishing capacity to generalize to longer and more difficult problem instances than those seen in training. However, theoretical understanding of this phenomenon still lags behind. Unlike most machine learning models, the generalisation abilities of transformers inherently require considering two axes. On one hand, one must examine in-distribution statistical generalisation, which concerns the ability of a model to broaden a function from training samples to novel samples of the same distribution. On the other hand, given the sequential nature of language data, one must also consider length generalisation, which reflects whether a model trained on inputs of a given length can extrapolate to longer ones.These two notions have mostly been studied separately, leaving open how they interact. translated_title: 多层Transformer的定量泛化界：少数长字符串可以胜过大量短字符串
translated_abstract: 基于Transformer的语言模型展现出惊人的能力，能够泛化到比训练中所见更长、更难的问题实例。然而，对这一现象的理论理解仍然滞后。与大多数机器学习模型不同，Transformer的泛化能力本质上需要从两个维度进行考察。一方面，必须研究分布内统计泛化，即模型将从训练样本学到的函数拓展到来自同一分布的新样本的能力；另一方面，鉴于语言数据的序列特性，还必须考虑长度泛化，即在给定长度输入上训练的模型能否外推到更长的输入。这两个概念以往大多被分开研究，它们之间如何相互作用仍是一个悬而未决的问题。在这项工作中，我们对固定精度的Transformer给出了两个维度的联合分析。我们给出了一般……
tldr: 本文首次对固定精度多层Transformer的分布内统计泛化与长度泛化进行了联合的定量理论分析，并揭示出一个反直觉的结论：用少数长字符串训练可以胜过用大量短字符串训练。
